newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market quiet, no bid-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market quiet, no bid-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Thursday were extremely quiet, with no reported bids as the industry gets squared away for the three-day Memorial Day holiday weekend, feedlot sources said.
If bids do surface, they were expected at $66.00 per cwt, steady with limited sales on Wednesday.
Several cattle feeders said they had sold out their showlists this week, and others that had a few cattle remaining were pricing them at $67.00.
"Probably not much going to happen the rest of this week," a Texas Panhandle feedlot manager said.

The bulk of this week's cattle sold Tuesday at $67.00 in active trading, with further sales on Wednesday at $66.00 for a small number of cattle that may have been of lower quality than cattle sold Tuesday, sources said.
There were a few reports of packers picking up cattle early Thursday that had been purchased on Monday.

Weekend slaughter was expected to be light and no major U.S. beef plant will be open on Monday in observance of Memorial Day. Demand following the holiday was seen moderate as packers start lining up cattle for the next week, several sources said.
